Mixed-effects fit by marginal maximum likelihood

Source: R/EM.R
em.Rd

Fits a mixed-effects model: the random effects that insert() with effect formulas put into the parameter transformation are integrated out, and the fixed parameters and the hyperparameters of the random effects are estimated by maximizing the marginal likelihood.

A group, a level of the grouping of a random term such as a patient or a cell line, may own several conditions, which share the random effects of the group. Normal, spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects of one grouping may be combined. Random terms over several groupings, nested or crossed, are normal and integrated per connected component of the conditions.

Methods:

"focei"

Laplace approximation at the conditional modes with the exact derivative of the volume term. The default, and the method for several groupings; also for spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects (at most 14 groups).

"quadrature"

adaptive sparse-grid quadrature around the modes, started from the FOCEI fit; section Quadrature. Also for spike-and-slab random effects alone, per subset; section Sparse random effects.

"laplaceEM"

ECM on the Laplace approximation with the covariance-corrected update of Omega.

"saem"

stochastic-approximation EM, also for spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects; section SAEM. With many structural parameters and sparse random effects it does not find the optimum from random starts reliably; start it from a "focei" fit, em(obj, random, fit, method = "saem"), to check that fit without the Laplace approximation.

Usage

em(
  obj,
  random,
  init = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  method = c("focei", "quadrature", "laplaceEM", "saem"),
  control = list(),
  cores = 1L,
  verbose = TRUE,
  sparse = "auto"
)

Arguments

obj

Objective of the data, normL2() or normT() of the model g * x * p, without terms for the random effects.

random

The random effects, randomEffects() of the parameter transformation or of p.

init

Named numeric start with the parameters of obj that are neither random effects nor created by the effect formulas (those start at 0). It may also set those and the hyperparameters: omega_<a>_<a>, the log of the diagonal entry of the Cholesky factor of Omega (the log standard deviation of an uncorrelated random effect), and omega_<a>_<b>, the entry in row a and column b below the diagonal, with a and b the stems of the random effects without eta_, as in omega_cl_cl; prob_* and tau_* (spike and slab), concentration_* and tau_* (Dirichlet process), named <kind>_<grouping> and numbered _1, _2, ... where a grouping has several blocks. An em fit as init gives the start: the estimates, fixed values and random effects of that fit, without those it set to 0, and with sparse random effects the inner modes.

fixed

Named numeric of parameters held fixed.

method

"focei" (default), "quadrature", "laplaceEM" or "saem".

control

List of options; other entries are an error.

sd

start of the standard deviations of the random effects, default 0.3.

inner

"nested" (default) solves the modes at every evaluation of the outer search; "sqp" takes sqpIterlim iterations of the inner search from the modes predicted along d eta / d theta, with value and gradient corrected to first order for the eta gradient left over, until the outer search stops, and then goes on nested from there, so that the estimates are those of the nested search. Applies to FOCEI and to spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects.

innerControl

the trust region of the modes: rinit and rmax, the initial and largest radius (default 1 and 10); iterlim, default 30 and over several groupings 100; steptol, default 1e-8, the Newton step at which it stops; mtol, default 1e-12, the predicted change of -2 log L, relative to -2 log L, at which a step on the boundary of the region stops it; eigenFloorRelative, default 1e-10, the floor of the eigenvalues of the inner Hessian relative to their mean (one grouping); sqpIterlim, default 2, the inner iterations per evaluation with inner = "sqp". With spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects only sqpIterlim applies. Other entries are an error.

trustControl

the outer trust region; it stops where the predicted change of -2 log L is below mtol, default 1e-5. Takes ftol, mtol, gtol and xtol flat or in tolControl. With random effects over several groupings the outer search is trust(), and every argument of trust() passes, hessianMethod, phases and qnControl included; FOCEI of one grouping reads rinit, rmax, iterlim, ftol and mtol. Other entries are an error.

secondOrderCorrection

the derivative of the volume term, default TRUE.

derivMode

how FOCEI gets the second derivatives of the volume term: "forward-reverse" (default), sweeps for models built with derivMode = c("reverse", "forward-reverse"), or "forward-forward", the second-order sensitivities of models built with derivMode = "forward-forward". Without the mode asked for the fit takes the other, with a message.

boundary

the largest rise of -2 log L at which a variance is set to 0, default 0.1, FALSE for none. With one grouping and several blocks, a normal random effect that forms a block alone and whose standard deviation ends below 0.1 is dropped and the fit repeated from the estimates; where -2 log L rises by at most boundary, that fit is returned and names the hyperparameter in boundary.

quadrature, saem, sparseFit

lists of the sections Quadrature, SAEM and Sparse random effects; other entries are an error.

cores

Number of cores over the groups and conditions inside the fit; with 1 (default) no threads are started.

verbose

Logical; print the progress of the iterative methods. Default TRUE.

sparse

"auto" (default), TRUE or FALSE: the outer trust region of FOCEI over normal random effects on the sparse Gauss-Newton Hessian. "auto" decides as trust() does.

Value

An object of class em with, among others:

argument, value, gradient, hessian

the estimates, -2 log L of the marginal likelihood with gradient and Hessian (a sparse Matrix on the sparse path, NULL with spike-and-slab or Dirichlet-process random effects); on the sparse path lowrank, the part of the Hessian kept apart (see objlist()).

information

with spike-and-slab random effects the empirical information that gives the standard errors: G / (G - 1) times the sum of the outer products of the centered scores of the G groups, of rank at most G - 1, plus half the curvature of the terms without random effects (conditions outside every group, priors) by their expected information (hessian = "expected", see dModfn), positive semidefinite. It is not the Hessian of the marginal -2 log L and is singular where the scores and those terms span fewer directions than there are parameters. vcov() inverts it where it is positive definite.

converged, iterations

the convergence of the outer search and the iterations; with several groupings also phaseIterations of trust().

innerIterations, sqpIterations

with FOCEI and sparse random effects the iterations of the inner searches summed over the groups and evaluations, and with control$inner = "sqp" the outer iterations on inexact modes.

Omega, omega

the covariance of the normal random effects, their standard deviations and correlations with standard errors.

random

per group the modes with conditional standard errors; for spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects also the cluster, 0 for the population value, and the posterior probability p0 of a deviation of 0; a column data where a sparse random effect reaches no data of the group; such an effect rests at 0 with the prior.

slab

the hyperparameters of the spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process blocks.

valueSE

the standard error of value where it comes from importance sampling.

coupling

"expectationConsistent" where a group needed it, else NULL.

boundary

the hyperparameters set to 0, see control.

etaModes, etaSE, shrinkage

the modes of the random effects per group, their conditional standard errors, and per random effect 1 - SD(modes) / SD from Omega.

certificate

with method "quadrature" per group the importance-sampling check at the estimate, section Quadrature.

Methods: print, summary, coef, vcov, confint, logLik, residuals, predict, plot.

Quadrature

Method "quadrature" alternates between placing the nodes around the modes at the current parameters and one trust step over every parameter on these frozen nodes. The nodes of the mu-referenced fixed effects are frozen in phi = X beta + eta. Entries of control$quadrature:

tol

allowed change of -2 log L by the next refinement, default 0.1, split over the groups. Each group starts from the Smolyak grid of the stage and the grid of the last rebuild, and refines it dimension-adaptively (Gerstner and Griebel 2003): the forward neighbors of the grid are evaluated, their change of -2 log L is the error, and the neighbor of largest change joins the grid until the error is within tol / G. A grid therefore refines only the directions in which the integrand departs from the Gaussian at the mode. Where the next refinement exceeds maxNodes, the evaluated neighbors join the grid and their change is the estimate. Inf keeps the grids of the stages.

levels

the stages, default K + 1 with K the number of random effects of a group; level K + s integrates polynomials of total degree 2 s + 1 exactly.

maxLevel, maxNodes

highest level, default K + 8, and the largest number of evaluated nodes per group, default 1000; the level of an adaptive grid is that of the smallest Smolyak grid holding it. A group whose error exceeds tol / G at the highest level within both is capped. Column capped of stageTrace counts the capped groups; attribute "levels" of stageTrace and the certificate list level, level error and cap per group.

tolDecrement

a stage ends when a Newton step on the rebuilt nodes would lower -2 log L by less than this, default 1e-4 (stopReason "decrement"), or when -2 log L rose after a step on nodes of unchanged levels, so the step lies below what the levels resolve ("resolution"). converged means stationary at the levels reached, capped ones included; the fit returns the iterate of lowest -2 log L on the highest levels.

maxEcmPerStage, cm1Control, maxCm1Iter

rebuilds per stage (default 10, stopReason "iterlim" where they run out), trust() settings and iterations of a step (default 30).

pruneTol

nodes whose weight lies this much in log below the largest are dropped, default Inf.

certificate

FALSE, or a list of points (default 256) and seed (default 1): importance sampling at the estimate from a t5 proposal at the mode of each group. A group is flagged where the two -2 log L differ by more than three standard errors plus the error the level of the group allows, or the Pareto shape of the weights exceeds 0.7.

epsEcm, maxEcm

for "laplaceEM": the extrapolated distance to the fixed point at which it stops, default 1e-5, and the iteration limit, default 200.

SAEM

Metropolis draws of the random effects by random-walk and independence proposals at the conditional modes, Robbins-Monro averages of their sufficient statistics, the mu-referenced fixed effects and Omega in closed form, the other parameters by Newton steps on averaged quadratic models. Entries of control$saem:

nBurnin, nEM

at most that many burn-in and averaging iterations, default 200 and 300.

nMcmc, nLaplace

random-walk and independence steps per iteration, default 3 each; nLaplace with normal random effects alone.

laplaceEvery, laplaceScale

iterations between refreshes of the modes, default 5, with normal random effects alone, and the factor of the proposal covariance, default 1.5, also of the slab value of an indicator move.

window, mcTol

the burn-in ends when no parameter has a significant slope over the last window iterations (default 25), the averaging when the expected rise of -2 log L from the Monte Carlo error is below mcTol (default 0.05).

particles

the particles of the sequential importance sampling of -2 log L with Dirichlet-process random effects, default 500.

cm1Control

trust() settings of the Newton steps of the other parameters, default one iteration per SAEM iteration.

nFlip

with spike-and-slab random effects the sweeps over the indicators per iteration, default 1.

nodes

Gauss-Hermite nodes of the slab mass of an indicator, 3 (default) or 5.

integral

"importance" takes -2 log L by importance sampling over the partitions also where Dirichlet-process random effects beside spike-and-slab ones allow the exact sum.

With normal random effects alone, -2 log L at the estimate is the quadrature of level K + 2, and maxLevel, maxNodes and pruneTol of control$quadrature apply to it. With spike-and-slab or Dirichlet-process random effects the averaging runs nEM iterations. A sweep of Metropolis-Hastings moves visits every indicator of a group once, in random order and for all groups at once, with the slab value integrated out: the other slab values of the group follow along the regression of the local quadratic model of the data, the slab mass on that line is a Gauss-Hermite sum with the exact model at the nodes, and the proposal draws the indicator from the resulting conditional inclusion probability and the slab value from the local Gaussian; the independence Metropolis-Hastings step keeps the posterior exact. nMcmc random-walk steps move the slab values of every group jointly. prob and tau follow in closed form from the averaged conditional inclusion probabilities and slab second moments of the sweeps, not from the drawn indicators; an estimated tau starts at least at the largest group mode under the slab alone. An em fit as init starts the chain at the selected random effects of that fit instead, the way to check a FOCEI optimum by SAEM. The acceptance rates of births, deaths and random-walk steps per iteration are columns of stageTrace. A Gibbs sweep draws the clusters of the Dirichlet-process random effects (Neal 2000, algorithm 8). The reported clusters are the most frequent partition of the late draws, a spike-and-slab random effect is selected where the mean conditional inclusion probability of the late sweeps is above 1/2, p0 one minus that mean. -2 log L is that of method = "focei" at the estimate; with Dirichlet-process random effects alone, or beside spike-and-slab ones on more than 14 groups, by importance sampling over the partitions, with valueSE.

Sparse random effects

With spike-and-slab random effects of the default spike = 0, mean = 0 or Dirichlet-process random effects, method = "focei" moves the parameters and hyperparameters in one trust region. The integral of a group is exact where the data couple none of the factors and the sum over the subsets of the spike-and-slab random effects of the group stays within a budget of nodes; else it is the expectation consistent (EC) approximation, and a trial point at which EC does not converge is a failed evaluation. Entries of control$sparseFit:

maxOuter

iterations of the trust region, default 200.

trustControl

the trust() settings of the outer search. The modes are found as by FOCEI, by the group kernel, where the Gauss-Newton step is below 1e-8; of control$innerControl only sqpIterlim applies.

maxEcm, epsEcm, budget, ec

of the sum over subsets, see below.

Spike-and-slab random effects with mean or spike other than 0, see spikeSlab(), take a separate path of method = "focei", beside normal random effects of the same grouping but no Dirichlet-process ones. The integral of a group is the sum over all subsets of the spike-and-slab random effects, each subset a Laplace integral over the normal random effects and the slab ones of the subset at the inner mode, the other random effects at the spike; spike = -Inf switches the parameter off. The number of subsets summed over all groups is at most budget (default 4096). The fixed effects and hyperparameters follow by EM: prob is the mean inclusion probability, tau^2 the mean squared deviation from mean under the slab, and the fixed effects minimize the data term plus slab prior summed over the subsets with their weights, jointly with the subset modes; the log determinant of the Laplace integral enters the weights only; Omega is the mean of the posterior second moments of the normal random effects, restricted to the block structure. EM stops after maxEcm iterations (default 200) or when no estimate changes by more than epsEcm (default 1e-6). The p0 column of the random table is the posterior probability of the spike.

method = "saem" draws them by the moves of section SAEM: a spike at -Inf leaves the other slab values as they are, and a move into the slab proposes from the Laplace approximation of the coordinate given the others, by Newton steps on the model. The reported -2 log L is the sum over subsets of method = "focei" at the estimate; Dirichlet-process random effects beside are refused.

method = "quadrature" takes the same path for every model with spike-and-slab random effects, the default spike = 0 included, after EM on the Laplace integrals to their fixed point. Every subset of Laplace weight above 1e-8 of the largest is integrated on a dimension-adaptive sparse grid around the inner mode as in section Quadrature; a group has control$quadrature$tol / G (default 0.1 / G), a subset of relative weight \(w\) the share \(1 / w\) of it, so that light subsets stay on the first grid; the other subsets keep the Laplace value. Then every parameter, the Cholesky parameters of Omega and the estimated prob and tau included, moves by trust steps on the frozen nodes, which are rebuilt after each step until a Newton step would lower -2 log L by less than tolDecrement (stopReason "decrement"). Of control$quadrature this path reads tol, maxLevel and maxNodes (per subset), tolDecrement, maxEcmPerStage, cm1Control and maxCm1Iter.

Groups beyond the budget, the largest first, take the expectation consistent (EC) approximation in a coordinate in which the spike is 0: the rate \(b^\eta\) for spike = -Inf, where the slab is log-normal, and \(\eta\) minus the spike else. The data term is a Gaussian in that coordinate, expanded first at the mode with every random effect in the slab and again at the EC mean until it is stable; normal random effects enter it exactly, without sites. These groups take the subset of inclusion probability above 1/2 for the fixed effects. Entries of control$sparseFit$ec: nodes of the Gauss-Hermite rule of the log-normal slab (40), maxSweeps (500) and tolSweep (1e-5, the change of the marginal means in standard deviations), maxRelinearize (30) and tolRelinearize (1e-4, relative).

See also

msem(), randomEffects(), insert(); the guide chapters Nonlinear mixed-effects models and Sparse deviations, the methods articles Marginal likelihood of mixed-effects models and Sparsity priors.

Examples

# \donttest{
## Theophylline, 12 subjects: one-compartment model with first-order absorption in closed
## form, log parameters with a normal random intercept per subject, additive error
th <- datasets::Theoph
th$Subject <- as.character(th$Subject)
subjects <- unique(th$Subject)
data <- as.datalist(data.frame(name = "y", time = th$Time, value = th$conc, sigma = NA_real_,
                               condition = th$Subject))
## second derivatives forward over reverse, the default of em()
dm <- c("forward", "reverse", "forward-reverse")
x <- Xt()
g <- Y(c(y = "amt * Ka / (V * Ka - Cl) * (exp(-Cl / V * time) - exp(-Ka * time))"),
       states = "time", modelname = "theoph_obs", compile = FALSE, derivMode = dm,
       outdir = tempdir())
#> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpJDzFHt/theoph_obs.cpp
err <- Y(c(y = "sigma_add"), g, attachInput = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_err", compile = FALSE,
         derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir())
#> Overwriting: /tmp/RtmpJDzFHt/theoph_err.cpp
## one condition per subject with the subject dose; the effect formula replaces each log parameter
## by an intercept plus a random effect per subject
doses <- tapply(th$Dose * th$Wt, th$Subject, `[`, 1)[subjects]
trafo <- branch(define(NULL, "x <- x", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "amt", "sigma_add")),
                table = data.frame(ID = subjects, dose = doses, row.names = subjects))
trafo <- insert(trafo, "amt <- dose", dose = dose)
trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("Ka", "V", "Cl", "sigma_add"))
p <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + V + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)), method = "explicit", compile = FALSE,
       modelname = "theoph_p", derivMode = dm, outdir = tempdir())
compile(g, err, p, output = tempfile("theoph"))
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC]
#> reusing 14 unchanged object(s)
obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = err)
init <- c(Ka = 0, V = 3, Cl = 0.7, sigma_add = log(0.5))

## FOCEI fit, the estimates and the random effects per subject
fit <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init)
fit
#> EM (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations, 12 groups
#>          Ka           V          Cl   sigma_add omega_Ka_Ka   omega_V_V 
#>   0.4638825   3.4597479   1.0121568  -0.3647014  -0.4552240  -1.9774269 
#> omega_Cl_Cl 
#>  -1.3361153 
#> Random effects:
#>  type eta1 eta2  estimate         se
#>    sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302
#>    sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699
#>    sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477
summary(fit)
#> EM summary (focei): -2 log L 359.403186, converged TRUE, 10 iterations
#>   without the 2 pi constant of the data (NONMEM OBJ): 116.803413
#> 
#> Parameters:
#>             estimate      se rsePct
#> Ka            0.4639 0.19180 41.350
#> V             3.4600 0.04718  1.364
#> Cl            1.0120 0.08333  8.233
#> sigma_add    -0.3647 0.07268 19.930
#> omega_Ka_Ka  -0.4552 0.23600 51.850
#> omega_V_V    -1.9770 0.29440 14.890
#> omega_Cl_Cl  -1.3360 0.25060 18.750
#> Standard errors without the curvature of the prediction in the random effects within the volume term (forward over reverse; derivMode = "forward-forward" gives the full one)
#> 
#> Random effects:
#>  type eta1 eta2 estimate      se
#>    sd   Ka   Ka   0.6343 0.14970
#>    sd    V    V   0.1384 0.04076
#>    sd   Cl   Cl   0.2629 0.06586
#> 
#> Shrinkage: eta_Ka = 0.018, eta_V = 0.103, eta_Cl = 0.039 
fit$omega
#>   type eta1 eta2  estimate         se
#> 1   sd   Ka   Ka 0.6343058 0.14972302
#> 2   sd    V    V 0.1384250 0.04075699
#> 3   sd   Cl   Cl 0.2628648 0.06586477
head(fit$random)
#>   group eta parameter        mode        se
#> 1     1  Ka  eta_Ka_1  0.08621976 0.1515854
#> 2     2  Ka  eta_Ka_2  0.19818408 0.1725709
#> 3     3  Ka  eta_Ka_3  0.37186008 0.1810720
#> 4     4  Ka  eta_Ka_4 -0.28173371 0.1640986
#> 5     5  Ka  eta_Ka_5 -0.04271272 0.1461175
#> 6     6  Ka  eta_Ka_6 -0.38568935 0.2043190

## quadrature started from the FOCEI estimates, and SAEM
fitQ <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = fit, method = "quadrature", verbose = FALSE)
fitS <- em(obj, randomEffects(p), init = init, method = "saem", verbose = FALSE)
c(focei = fit$value, quadrature = fitQ$value, saem = fitS$value)
#>      focei quadrature       saem 
#>   359.4032   360.7089   360.7757 
# }
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Ka and Cl with correlated random effects, V with a spike-and-slab one: a second transformation
p2 <- P(insert(trafo, Ka + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | p | ID), V ~ 1 + (1 | gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab()))),
        method = "explicit", compile = FALSE, modelname = "theoph_p2", derivMode = dm,
        outdir = tempdir())
compile(p2, output = tempfile("theoph"))
fit2 <- em(normL2(data, g * x * p2, errmodel = err), randomEffects(p2), init = init)
fit2$omega
fit2$slab
AIC(fit, fit2)
} # }
